title: Ha eller få — having or receiving
goal: Choose ha for possession and få for receiving or acquiring something.

objectives.statement: Choose ha for possession and få for receiving or acquiring something.

sections.title: A new key at the office

spans.value: Nora has recently started a new job. On Monday morning, she meets her colleague Henrik near the entrance.

blocks.translation: Do you have a key to the main entrance?

spans.value: Ja, jeg har nøkkel. Fikk du ikke en på fredag?

blocks.translation: Yes, I have a key. Didn’t you get one on Friday?

spans.value: Nei. Jeg fikk adgangskort, men jeg fikk ikke nøkkel.

blocks.translation: No. I got an access card, but I didn’t get a key.

spans.value: Da må du snakke med Fatima. Hun har nøklene til de nye ansatte.

blocks.translation: Then you need to talk to Fatima. She has the keys for the new employees.

spans.value: Får jeg nøkkelen med én gang?

blocks.translation: Will I get the key straight away?

spans.value: Sannsynligvis. Når du får den, kan du ha den på samme nøkkelknippe som husnøkkelen.

blocks.translation: Probably. When you get it, you can keep it on the same key ring as your house key.

spans.value: A few minutes later, Nora finds Fatima.
Hei, Fatima. Jeg har adgangskort, men jeg har ikke nøkkel til hoveddøra.

blocks.translation: Hi, Fatima. I have an access card, but I don’t have a key to the main entrance.

spans.value: Det stemmer. Du får nøkkelen nå.

blocks.translation: That’s right. You’re getting the key now.

spans.value: Takk! Nå har jeg både kort og nøkkel.

blocks.translation: Thanks! Now I have both a card and a key.

That contrast is the focus of this chapter:

items.value: describes possession: someone has or possesses something.
describes receiving or acquiring something: something comes into someone’s possession.

spans.value: when the important point is that a person possesses something or has it available.

en.value: Henrik has a key.
Nora has an access card.
Fatima has the keys.

spans.value: These sentences describe a current situation. They do not tell us when or how Henrik, Nora, or Fatima obtained the objects.
The negative form works in the same way:

en.value: Nora does not have a key.
We do not have any coffee.
Amir does not have a car.
Do you have a pen?
Do you have tickets?

no.value: Har hun en kopi av kontrakten?

en.value: Does she have a copy of the contract?

spans.value: In each case, the speaker wants to know what is already in someone’s possession or available to them.

when the important point is that someone receives or acquires something. The object was not in that person’s possession before, but it comes to them.

en.value: Nora gets a key.

no.value: Vi får nye datamaskiner på kontoret.

en.value: We are getting new computers at the office.
The children are getting ice cream after dinner.

spans.value: Compare this with a question using

en.value: Do you have the package?

The easiest way to understand the contrast is to follow one object across time.

en.value: Nora does not have a key.

no.value: Nora får en nøkkel av Fatima.

en.value: Nora gets a key from Fatima.
Now Nora has a key.

spans.value: The middle sentence marks the acquisition. The first and third describe possession at different times.
Here is the same pattern with a package:

en.value: I do not have the package yet.
I am getting the package this afternoon.
Now I have the package.

en.value: He gets two tickets from a friend.
Afterwards, he has two tickets.

Study these pairs. Each pair refers to the same kind of object, but the viewpoint changes.

en.value: Lea has five hundred kroner.

no.value: Lea får fem hundre kroner for arbeidet.

en.value: Lea gets five hundred kroner for the work.

spans.value: The first sentence describes the money Lea possesses. The second describes money coming to her as payment.

no.value: Vi har et rom på hotellet.

en.value: We have a room at the hotel.

no.value: Vi får et rom med utsikt.

en.value: We are getting a room with a view.

spans.value: The first sentence describes the reservation or room available to us. The second focuses on which room is assigned to us.

en.value: Daniel has the report.
Daniel will get the report after the meeting.

spans.value: One sentence tells us where the report is now. The other tells us when it will come to Daniel.

en.value: Mina has a new watch.

no.value: Mina fikk en ny klokke til bursdagen.

en.value: Mina got a new watch for her birthday.

spans.value: The first sentence describes current possession. The second presents the watch as something she received.

no.value: Jeg har en plass ved vinduet.

en.value: I have a seat by the window.

no.value: Jeg fikk en plass ved vinduet.

en.value: I got a seat by the window.

spans.value: describes the seat that is mine or available to me now.
tells us that the seat was assigned or given to me.

This checkpoint matters because choosing the right verb is not only a matter of recognizing vocabulary. The learner must be able to view the same situation first as a change and then as a resulting state. A successful response would demonstrate a consistent shift from acquisition to possession without changing the basic facts.

sections.title: Sources and times often support få

spans.value: often includes information about where something comes from or when it arrives.

no.value: Jeg fikk boka av en venn.

en.value: I got the book from a friend.
Nora gets the key from Fatima.

no.value: Vi får svar fra banken i morgen.

en.value: We will get an answer from the bank tomorrow.
They got the package on Monday.

spans.value: fit naturally with an event of receiving.
However, these expressions are clues, not mechanical rules. The meaning still decides the verb.

en.value: I have the book from the course.

spans.value: This sentence describes the book currently in my possession.
identifies it; it does not necessarily describe the moment I received it.
can contain a time expression if it describes possession during that time.

en.value: I have the car all week.

spans.value: The speaker possesses or has use of the car throughout the week. Nothing in the sentence focuses on acquiring it.
Using ha for the moment of receiving

no.value: Jeg har en gave fra kollegaene mine i går.

en.value: I have a gift from my colleagues yesterday.

spans.value: Suppose the intended situation is that the colleagues handed the gift to the speaker yesterday. That explicit context establishes a receiving event;
only locates it in time and does not by itself determine the choice between possession and acquisition. In this example, the receiving event is expressed with

no.value: Jeg fikk en gave fra kollegaene mine i går.

en.value: I got a gift from my colleagues yesterday.

spans.value: If the speaker wants to describe present possession,
is appropriate, but the sentence needs a present-state meaning:

no.value: Jeg har en gave fra kollegaene mine på kontoret.

en.value: I have a gift from my colleagues at the office.

spans.value: Using få for something already possessed

en.value: I get the key in my pocket.

spans.value: If the intended meaning is that the key is currently in the speaker’s possession and located in the pocket, use

en.value: I have the key in my pocket.

spans.value: For the possession-versus-receiving contrast taught here, use
when the intended meaning is that the speaker receives the key. Other constructions with
is not inherently ungrammatical outside the intended static-possession reading:

en.value: I get the key from the receptionist.

spans.value: Treating får as a general replacement for har
has many uses, but in this lesson
is tied to receiving or acquiring something. Do not choose
merely because an English translation could contain

en.value: Do you have a ticket?

spans.value: This asks whether the ticket is already in the person’s possession.

en.value: Are you getting a ticket?

spans.value: This asks whether a ticket will come to the person.
Once a person receives an object, the next description normally changes to

no.value: I går fikk jeg et nytt adgangskort. Nå har jeg det i lommeboka.

en.value: Yesterday I got a new access card. Now I have it in my wallet.

spans.value: would continue to present new receiving events. It would not simply describe the card remaining in the wallet.

sections.title: Practice: follow an object through a day

spans.value: Picture a hotel guest named Elias. In the morning, he arrives without a room key. At reception, an employee hands him one. Later, he keeps it in his jacket pocket. In the evening, he cannot find it and asks whether his travel companion possesses it.
Describe the key at each stage using the supplied present forms

This practice brings together the two viewpoints in a fresh setting while keeping the same communicative problem as Nora’s office key. A successful response would demonstrate that the learner can follow one object through changing circumstances and select the verb according to possession or acquisition at each moment.
Return to the office. Nora is waiting for a computer, a parking permit, and a copy of her contract. Some items have already arrived; others are due later.
Form questions that distinguish these two needs:

items.value: finding out whether Nora currently possesses an item;
finding out whether Nora will receive an item.

spans.value: Then give short replies that preserve the same distinction.

prompt.value: Use the office facts to complete the Norwegian restatements. Nora possesses the key, Henrik does not possess the key, and Fatima possesses the access card. Choose the supplied form that matches each current situation.

Complete each Norwegian sentence about an office transfer. Fatima hands Nora a key, a colleague hands Nora a document, and an employee delivers a new chair. Use the form that describes receiving rather than resulting possession.

explanation.value: «få» presents the moment of receiving or obtaining something; «ha» presents the resulting state of possession.

prompt.value: For each situation, complete the first receiving frame and the second resulting-possession frame. Keep each object and basic fact unchanged while shifting viewpoint from receiving to possession.

Write a 4–5 sentence present-tense sequence in Norwegian about Elias and one hotel room key. Include these stages: in the morning Elias does not have the key; at reception he receives it; later the key is in his jacket pocket; in the evening state whether his travel companion has the key. Use har ikke or har for possession and får for the receiving event. Keep the same key and situation throughout.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the Norwegian sequence against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Accept natural Bokmål wording when it preserves the required forms, meaning, and timeline.

criteria.instruction: Uses har or har ikke for Elias's possession or non-possession at the required stages.
Uses får for the moment when Elias receives the room key at reception.
Keeps the same room key, people, and timeline consistent throughout.

prompt.value: Write three short question-and-reply pairs in Norwegian about Nora's computer, parking permit, and copy of the contract. Use all three items. Include a pair about current possession and a pair about receiving or acquiring an item. Start the possession question with Har Nora ...? and the receiving question with Får Nora ...?; give a short reply to each question that keeps the same viewpoint.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the questions and replies against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Accept natural Bokmål wording and equivalent item phrases when the required viewpoint and verb distinction remain clear.

criteria.instruction: Includes a question beginning exactly with Har Nora ...? that asks about current possession.
Includes a question beginning exactly with Får Nora ...? that asks about receiving or acquiring an item.
Gives a short reply to each question while preserving the distinction between possession and receiving.

prompt.value: Select the verb that does not fit the receiving situation.

payload.feedback: Replace har with får. Henrik is handing Nora the document now, so the corrected sentence describes acquisition rather than possession.

prompt.value: First write one or two Norwegian sentences explaining the difference between ha and få. Then write a short present-tense sequence in Norwegian about one new everyday object in one consistent situation. Use the exact viewpoint order har ikke, then får, then har. Keep the object and situation unchanged.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the Norwegian explanation and the Norwegian sequence separately. Report evidence for each criterion. Accept natural wording and equivalent new objects when the meaning and required verb order are preserved.

criteria.instruction: The Norwegian explanation distinguishes possession from receiving or acquiring.
The Norwegian sequence keeps one object and situation consistent.
The Norwegian sequence uses har ikke first, får next, and har finally, with each verb matching its situation.
